description: Classification of the preserved historical examples in legacy/examples/ for issue #14. These files are review inputs from the pre-contract legacy draft, byte-pinned by sha256; do not repair them in place. Each entry records how the file behaves against legacy/fht-v0.1.json when validated with jsonschema 4.26.0, Draft 2020-12 dialect, explicit FormatChecker (the procedure scripts/check_legacy_examples.py re-measures). Statuses: 'nonconforming-historical' = parses but fails the legacy schema with the recorded errors; 'unparseable-historical' = the header block cannot even be parsed as YAML; 'not-json-or-yaml-historical' = outside the supported example formats, preserved as a presentation artifact. None of these files is advertised as a valid example of anything; 'notes' list additional defects a schema cannot express (semantic mismatches, typos). The current FHT 1.0 examples live in examples/ and are tested by tests/test_examples.py.

reasons: Embeds JSON Schema keywords ($schema, $id) in a data instance the legacy draft forbids at top level.
Carries assemblySoftware and reuseConditions, which the legacy draft's property list does not define (they re-enter the family later, per the field decisions on specs/fht-field-decisions.md).
Checksum is prefixed 'md5:' and 36 characters: too short for the draft's own 44-character sha2 definition and not base64 charset.
masking value 'soft-masked' is not one of the draft's alternation words.
notes: taxon.uri points at taxonomy:9606 (Homo sapiens) while the record names 'Bombas huntii' — the unanchored pattern cannot catch a wrong-but-shaped URI; the genus is also misspelled (Bombus).
The 'schema' field ends '.../FHT.jso' (truncated); the legacy draft types it as a plain string, so the schema cannot catch it.
assemblyAuthor uses a 'url' key instead of 'uri'; nested objects do not close additionalProperties, so the typo is silently accepted (defect L5 in scripts/check_legacy_schema.py).

reasons: Same field-level defects as example.fht.json (without the embedded $schema/$id keys).
schemaVersion is the YAML integer 1 — valid against the legacy number typing, yet another sign these files predate the string '1.0' contract.
notes: taxon.uri 9606 mismatches 'Bombas huntii' as in the JSON instance.
metadataAuthor/assemblyAuthor uris are correct here, unlike the JSON instance's 'url' typo.

reasons: The ;~ header block, after prefix stripping, is not well-formed YAML: the metadataAuthor/assemblyAuthor list items indent 'uri:' inconsistently with the '- name:' line, so safe parsing fails before any schema validation.
Even if repaired, it would carry the same value-level defects as example.fht.yaml (md5 checksum, soft-masked).
notes: Sequence bytes and the taxon mismatch are preserved as historical; the current FASTA examples in examples/ show the supported ;~ block layout with verified checksums.

reasons: HTML microdata presentation artifact from the retired converter era; it is not a JSON or YAML instance, so the JSON-Schema lane does not apply. Kept so the recorded rendering history is not lost.
notes: The filename says 'fhr' while the itemtype is the FHT schema URL — a historical naming slip, left verbatim.
Contains 'Bomnas huntii' (typo of Bombus) and stray double quotes inside uri/url span values.
